title: Consumption, Premium and Dedicated plans: the cold-start arithmetic

videos.script: The first order of the morning takes seconds. The next one takes a few milliseconds. Nothing in the code changed between them. {{plans}} What changed is whether the app had somewhere to run, and that is the plan's decision. Azure has five ways to host a function app. They differ in how far they scale and how long a function may run. They also differ in whether they stop when idle, and in what you pay for. {{cold}} A plan that stops when idle has to start again for the next request. That start is the cold start. Azure finds an instance, starts the host, starts Python and imports your file. Only then does the first request run. {{measure}} You will time that on your own laptop, from docker run to the first answer. Then you will slow the import on purpose, and give the container a quarter of a processor. The numbers are the laptop's, and the shape is the lesson. {{money}} Last, the money. One meter bills the seconds your code runs. Another bills an instance whether anyone calls it or not. You will work out the request rate where the two cost the same. Below it, paying per request is cheaper. Above it, the instance is. And below it, an instance kept ready is something you buy for speed, not to save money.
